newsitem.title: USA: Smoking may lead to limb defects in babies.
newsitem.headline: Smoking may lead to limb defects in babies.

text.p: A Swedish study released on Wednesday found that a woman who smokes during pregnancy may increase the chance of giving birth to a baby with defective limbs.
Karin Kallen, a researcher at the University of Lund in Sweden, reported her findings in a study of more than 1 million Swedish women in the Journal of the American Public Health Association.

She studied 610 cases of limb reduction malformations among more than 1 million babies born between 1983 and 1993. Because of extensive Swedish health registry information, detailed information was available on whether and how much the women smoked early in pregnancy.
"The present study supports a connection between maternal smoking during pregnancy and all limb reduction malformations," she wrote.

Earlier studies had found similar trends, but this study was far larger and reached statistical significance. However, Kallen noted that more research was needed to rule out other possible explanations.
